newsitem.title: USA: Texas power prices hold steady in mild weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas power prices hold steady in mild weather.

text.p: Wholesale power prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) held steady amidst mild weather that was expected to last through the weekend, industry sources said.

Temperatures through much of Texas were again expected to reach highs in the mid 70s degrees Fahrenheit Thursday, although forecasts called for some below normal temperatures through the southern portion of the state from November 19 to 23.
Prices for peak, firm power for Friday delivery were talked steady at $25.25-26.25 per megawatt hour (MWh), the brokers and marketers said.
Non-firm peak power for Friday was assessed near $24.00, the sources said.
Off-peak non-firm ERCOT power was pegged at $14.00-16.00, while firm off-peak for Friday delivery was discussed near $18.00 per MWh.

December peak power was talked higher at $25.25-25.75 from a range of $24.25-24.75 on Wednesday, while January/February ERCOT power prices were assessed at $25.30-25.85 from $24.50-25.50 on Wednesday, the sources said.
